method.label: Split the square using a circle

annotationRationale: The solution converts the side-ordering event into two regions and computes their probability by area. Sector areas supply the decisive calculations; the perpendicular bisector, equilateral triangle, and Pythagorean theorem determine the needed angles and height.
sourceMethod: Follows the official quarter-circle and half-square decomposition. The auxiliary points and area decompositions are described explicitly, and a squared-distance comparison clarifies why the two regions are exactly the favorable set.

review.mathCheck: The favorable cases are exactly \(BP<AP<1\) in the right half and \(1<AP<BP\) in the left half. Their disjoint areas are \(\pi/6-\sqrt3/8\) and \(1/2-\pi/12-\sqrt3/8\). Boundaries have area zero. The probability is \((6+\pi-3\sqrt3)/12\approx0.329\), giving the required sum 25, choice A.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Solution 25 on pages 25–26. The two regions and sector-minus-triangle calculations match the supplied figure. The added squared-distance comparison and derivation of the height make the construction reconstructible without reproducing the figure.
review.annotationCheck: Geometric probability and sector area are appropriately assessed. Perpendicular-bisector properties, equilateral-triangle properties, and the Pythagorean theorem each support an explicit step. Both strict orderings, equality boundaries, and coefficient conditions are handled.
